title: meat
summary: An old food word whose meaning changed.
question: Did meat always mean the food it means today?
completion: Meat continues Old English mete, meaning food generally. Its meaning became narrower. Old Norse matr is a cousin; French viande and English meet follow other trails.
partner: A familiar word can carry a surprising history. Follow the evidence!
